title: The access-event codes of a dashboard read, the entry field list, the page bounds, the read index and the Flyway step are named in no source
source: Work Package _work/msr/wp/B2-P4-027.md (story line RWB-P4-E1063-APP, patterns DP01, DP06, DP07, DP09, DP10, DP11, DP13, DP15, DP17, DP19); _work/msr/context/P4.md (four provided REST operations, five tables, JOB-18, no event, no workflow); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md Appendix T-A.1 (API-P4-008 GET /admin/access-log with query user, from, to, event, page, size; API-P4-012 GET /me/session); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md A2.4 and A2.8
description: This slice records every read of the agent monitoring dashboard on the access log of rwb-access and answers it back. Six values the record and the read need are in no source: the access-event code of a dashboard read and the code of a refusal, the entry field list beyond the screen, the event code, the agent codes, the business date, the caller reference, the outcome and the time that this story states; the page bounds of the log read; the name of the read index on the record table; the accept date and version number of the one Flyway step of DP-15; and the parameter codes that carry the event codes and the page bounds. The two operations used are published already and carry no object set, so the object is an addition this story has to fix and record rather than copy.
evidence: Context pack P4 lists exactly four provided operations, five tables (delegation_limit, masking_rule, permission, role, role_conflict) and no access-entry table; TSD P4 v3 T-A.1 gives API-P4-008 the query members user, from, to, event, page and size and no object type, and API-P4-012 no field list; FSD P4 v3 A2.4 and A2.8 describe the event and its decision-log linkage in prose with no field catalogue; no read source names a record code for an access entry, a page bound, an index name, a migration version or a parameter code
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-access with the ledger owner
proposed: Fix the two event codes on the access-event list in force and publish them with the next version of the access-log contract of RWB-P4-E1039-CON; publish the entry field list and the page bounds with the same read; take the record code from the library's code set at build time; name the read index in the physical schema of rwb_access; and register the Flyway step and the two parameter codes in the service's own sequence and parameter set. Each is a line in one contract document, not a schema change and not a business value.

title: The Reporting right of the legacy story, the data-lake copy of the access rule, the event row of the service and the DP dependencies disagree with the target sources
source: Work Package _work/msr/wp/B2-P4-027.md (story line RWB-P4-E1063-APP: H = [], C = [RWB-P10-E1063-CON], I = [], X = [], patterns DP01, DP06, DP07, DP09, DP10, DP11, DP13, DP15, DP17, DP19); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md R3 and R5.5 (the dependency column of DP-06, DP-07, DP-09, DP-15 and DP-19); _work/msr/context/P4.md (service row, ownership rows, slides 4, 5, 8, 10 and 13); legacy RWB-E1-063 sections 7, 10, 12 and 17
section: RWB-P4-E1063-APP metadata rows 15 to 18, and sections 1, 3, 5, 8, 10, 12.2, 12.3 and 13
description: Four disagreements meet in this slice and none is settled by a higher source. (1) The legacy story names Reporting R as the right that opens the dashboard and RW-CASEOWN as the role refused for holding none, while the metric read of rwb-agent declares Rules and parameters R (RWB-P10-E1063-CON); TSD P4 T6.1 carries Rules and parameters, Reference data and Platform administration only, so the Reporting letters of the other roles are not stated anywhere even though LOV-CAPABILITY has 14 areas. (2) FSD P4 REQ-ACA-006 and NFR-042 require every read of the data lake copy to be logged, and DP-17 removes the lake and the copy, so the object of the rule has no target and the read of the served aggregate is recorded instead. (3) The ownership row of this service lists no event of its own and P4 stories state that no third event name exists, while DP-09 is in the pattern set of this key and the access entry has to leave the service for the reporting read model. (4) The DP table adds H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON and C RWB-P3-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON, and the Work Package H list is empty and its C list holds RWB-P10-E1063-CON only.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-063 section 10 gives RW-RISK and RW-COE Reporting R, RW-BIANAL Reporting CRUD and RW-PLATADM Platform administration U, and its X6 refuses RW-CASEOWN for want of Reporting; TSD P4 v3 T6.1 shows three area columns and gives RW-RISK Rules and parameters RA; RWB-P10-E1063-CON section 12.1 guards the metric read with Rules and parameters R; FSD P4 v3 A2.4 records 14 capability areas and AC-EXC-P4-004-02 names a Reporting column; FSD P4 v3 REQ-ACA-006 and TSD P4 NFR-042 name the data lake copy; context pack P4 records no P4 event and no P4 workflow; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 dependency column and the Work Package line as quoted
owner_role: Solution architect with the rwb-access and rwb-agent owners
proposed: Keep both rights as they stand: the route checks Reporting R from the permission rows before it asks for a metric row, and the metric read keeps Rules and parameters R at its owner; record the Reporting letters for the remaining roles in the matrix load. Replace the lake copy of the access rule with the access entry of the served read and correct REQ-ACA-006 and NFR-042 in the next FSD and TSD version. Let the entry ride the shared decision-record topic and keep the two access event names of the service untouched. Add the five platform contracts to H and the two rwb-case contracts to C in the dependency map at D1, and let the Build Sequence carry the correction rather than a parallel edit of the plan.
